text:
Sam: FYI noticing a persistent hit-rate delta between us-west and eu-west after yesterday's routing change. us-west avg prefix hit-rate 74%, eu-west 41%. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 :frowning:
Anya: whoa that's large. Are those numbers from the per-prefix window or global cache metric? any breakdown by prompt length?
Sam: per-prefix 5m sliding. Short prompts (<128 tokens) show the biggest gap. Longer prompts are similar across regions.
Mike: my first guess: routing policy is pinning by customer-region which prevents cross-region warm keys from being reused. The tweak we rolled yesterday added strict-region affinity for routing. :thinking:
Leila: we intentionally tightened affinity to reduce cross-region egress, but didn't account for KV cache cold penalties. Can you paste the routing policy snippet?
Sam: sure, current rule:
```
route_policy:
  prefer_local: true
  affinity: strict
  fallback: nearest_compatible
```
Anya: I profiled a sample of missed keys in eu-west. ~62% of misses had canonicalization differences (trailing whitespace or punctuation normalized differently by the client-side preprocessor). That plus strict affinity explains a lot.
Sam: hmm clients in eu-west are sending anchors with trailing spaces? Any quick fixes server-side?
Anya: we can add a lightweight canonicalizer in the prefix-key pipeline (trim + collapse-spaces + lower) as a stopgap. Perf cost looks ~0.3ms per request on p99.
Mike: alternative: relax affinity to prefer_local but allow cross-region read-on-miss (replicate-on-read). That would warm eu-west faster without immediate full replication.
Leila: replicate-on-read seems reasonable but watch egress. We can gate it by customer tier or by prefix popularity threshold to limit cost.
InfraBot: deploy started: //deploys/12345
OpsBot: alert suppressed for cache-drop-eu for 30m (manual suppression by Sam)
Sam: did a microbenchmark of current pipeline with and without canonicalizer. Results (p50/p95 added latency): base 8ms/19ms, +canonicalizer 9ms/19.5ms. Hit-rate delta narrowed in simulation from 74/41 -> 73/62 when allowing cross-region reads for cold keys.
Anya: those sim numbers are promising. Also saw that batching heuristics differ slightly by region due to different request arrival distributions — eu-west had smaller batches leading to slightly higher per-token overhead; contributes to p95 tail but not hit-rate directly.
Mike: action plan proposal:
- roll a lightweight canonicalizer in front of KV lookup (canary 5% traffic eu-west)
- enable replicate-on-read for prefixes with >500 qps global traffic or for first 10k unique keys observed in last hour
- experiment with prefer_local -> prefer_local_with_read_through fallback
Anyone object?
Leila: +1, but add egress cap: replicate-on-read should only allow X MB/s per-customer. I'll add a config flag.
Sam: I'll open a quick PR with canonicalizer and a config toggle. Also will add a Grafana panel showing cross-region read rate and egress by tier.
Anya: I'll run a deeper analysis on canonicalization root causes and try to produce a list of top 50 offending clients.
Mike: after canary, let's compare hit-rate delta and p95 latency. If good, we can roll to 100% with adjustments.
Sam: thanks all. bumping to #eng-sre for visibility :thumbsup:
Leila: leaving a reminder: we should coordinate kernel selection changes separately — any kernel-level perf tweaks need a separate ops window. This change is at the pipeline/routing layer.
Sam: noted. I'll schedule the canary for 02:00 UTC tomorrow and ping everyone. End of thread.
